description: Text-grounded retrieval benchmark for PDF physical pages 51–100 of OpenStax Calculus Volume 1
split_method: Fixed before retrieval evaluation: Q001–Q015 dev, Q016–Q020 test
filter_field_note: section metadata must be assigned from PDF section boundaries in the ingestion pipeline before filter queries can run

questions.question: What is a piecewise-defined function?
questions.expected_answer: A function defined by different formulas on different parts of its domain.
questions.evidence_quote: Sometimes a function is defined by different formulas on different parts of its domain.

questions.question: During what hours is the parking garage in Example 1.20 open?
questions.expected_answer: From 6 a.m. to midnight.
questions.evidence_quote: The parking garage is open from 6 a.m. to 12 midnight.

questions.question: What kind of transformation is produced by shifting a graph horizontally or vertically?
questions.expected_answer: A shift is a transformation of a function.
questions.evidence_quote: A shift, horizontally or vertically, is a type of transformation of a function.

questions.question: How is vertical scaling applied to a function graph?
questions.expected_answer: Multiply every output of the function by the same positive constant.
questions.evidence_quote: A vertical scaling of a graph occurs if we multiply all outputs of a function by the same positive constant.

questions.question: In Section 1.2, which part of a function is multiplied to perform horizontal scaling?
questions.expected_answer: The inputs of the function.
questions.evidence_quote: The horizontal scaling of a function occurs if we multiply the inputs by the same positive constant.

questions.question: When several graph transformations are combined, why must their order be considered?
questions.expected_answer: Because graph transformations must be performed in the correct order to obtain the related function graph.
questions.evidence_quote: it is important to transform the graph in the correct order.

questions.question: Name two physical phenomena that can be modeled by trigonometric functions.
questions.expected_answer: Sound waves and vibrations of strings (other accepted examples: alternating current and pendulum motion).
questions.evidence_quote: Trigonometric functions are used to model many phenomena, including sound waves, vibrations of strings

questions.question: Besides describing points on circles, what geometric relationship do trigonometric functions express?
questions.expected_answer: The relationship between the sides and angles of a triangle.
questions.evidence_quote: They also define the relationship among the sides and angles of a triangle.

questions.question: What is a trigonometric identity?
questions.expected_answer: An equation involving trigonometric functions that holds for all angles where the functions are defined.
questions.evidence_quote: A trigonometric identity is an equation involving trigonometric functions that is true for all angles for which the functions are defined.

questions.question: In Section 1.3, why should you avoid dividing both sides by an expression that could be zero when solving a trigonometric equation?
questions.expected_answer: That expression might be zero, so division may remove valid solutions.
questions.evidence_quote: we would miss some of the solutions of the original equation.

questions.question: Why are trigonometric functions called periodic functions?
questions.expected_answer: Their values repeat as angles go around the unit circle.
questions.evidence_quote: Consequently, the trigonometric functions are periodic functions.

questions.question: What real-world quantity can be modeled using a shifted sine curve?
questions.expected_answer: Hours of daylight as a function of the day of the year.
questions.evidence_quote: A shifted sine curve arises naturally when graphing the number of hours of daylight

questions.question: What is the fundamental purpose of an inverse function?
questions.expected_answer: It reverses, or undoes, the operation of the original function.
questions.evidence_quote: An inverse function reverses the operation done by a particular function.

questions.question: What does the horizontal line test say about a one-to-one function?
questions.expected_answer: Every horizontal line intersects its graph at most once.
questions.evidence_quote: A function is one-to-one if and only if every horizontal line intersects the graph of no more than once.

questions.question: How do the domain and range relate when finding the inverse of a one-to-one function?
questions.expected_answer: The inverse maps values in the original range back to values in the original domain.
questions.evidence_quote: The inverse function maps each element from the range of back to its corresponding element from the domain of

questions.question: How can restricting a function’s domain make it possible to define an inverse?
questions.expected_answer: Choose a subset of the original domain where the function is one-to-one.
questions.evidence_quote: However, we can choose a subset of the domain of such that the function is one-to-one.

questions.question: Why must the domain of a trigonometric function be restricted to define an inverse?
questions.expected_answer: Trigonometric functions are periodic and are not one-to-one over their full domains.
questions.evidence_quote: The six basic trigonometric functions are periodic, and therefore they are not one-to-one.

questions.question: What distinguishes an exponential function from a power function?
questions.expected_answer: An exponential function has a constant base and variable exponent; a power function has a constant exponent.
questions.evidence_quote: Exponential functions have constant bases and variable exponents.

questions.question: In Section 1.5, what kind of function is the inverse of an exponential function?
questions.expected_answer: A logarithmic function.
questions.evidence_quote: Therefore, it has an inverse function, called the logarithmic function with base

questions.question: According to the Richter scale example, how much more intense is magnitude 8 than magnitude 6?
questions.expected_answer: 100 times as intense.
questions.evidence_quote: the first earthquake is 100 times more intense than the second earthquake.
